items.title: Week of 2026-09-29: budget-constrained uncertainty and a reality check on run-to-run noise
items.summary: 7 new entries, 0 updates. The strongest is a minimax-optimal confidence-interval bound for repeated LLM evaluation under a fixed response budget, verified on a 16-model LiveCodeBench replay.

items.title: Week of 2026-10-05: decomposing leaderboard variance, and when judges rank right but measure wrong
items.summary: 4 new entries, 0 updates. The strongest decomposes agent-leaderboard variance into model, scaffold, and task-design components with a Bayesian model, finding that pooling benchmarks helps reliability more than adding tasks.

items.title: Week of 2026-10-12: anytime-valid leaderboard security, and a statistical recheck of METR's time horizons
items.summary: 5 new entries, 0 updates. The strongest extends anytime-valid leaderboard testing to adversarial rigging with certified corruption budgets, verified on a replay of 1.8 million Chatbot Arena votes.

items.title: Week of 2026-10-19: multicalibrating LLM judges, and the limits of statistical safety assurance
items.summary: 6 new entries, 0 updates. The strongest applies multicalibration to bound many LLM-judge biases at once, even unspecified ones, with theoretical conditions under which this improves rather than trades off accuracy.
